maria: noticed a sharp p95 spike in prod-serving-us-west2 around 12:14 UTC. p95 -> 980ms, p99 ~1.8s. Opening inc.

incident-bot: INC-4521 created by maria · severity: sev2 · runbook: /inc/4521

maria: initial logs show kernel-selection thrash + KV cache eviction storms. small excerpt:
```
[12:14:01] kernel_select: attn-opt -> generic (fallback)
[12:14:02] kvcache: evict tenant=video-ads-prod evicted=37MB
[12:14:03] latency_ms=980
```

sam: on it. profiler shows compile churn on attn kernels and high eviction rate for that tenant's prefix. looks like noisy neighbor -> batching collapse.

jin: can we flip a routing policy to steer video-ads-prod to smaller model variant or apply tenant-level throttle? I can push a feature-flag to stabilise kernel selection: `runtime.kernel_stable=true` for the host.

leo: I can set tenant throttle now. propose qps=12 and burst=3. running:
```
$ rctl set-tenant-rate video-ads-prod --qps 12 --burst 3
Applied to cluster us-west2
```

ana: caution: throttling changes batching shapes; keep an eye on throughput for other tenants. Also KV pinning helps — I can bump pin-size for that tenant to 64MB.

sam: good call. applying KV pinning and increasing KV cache reservation for video-ads-prod.

maria: plan: 1) leo applied throttle (done) 2) ana increased KV pinning (done) 3) jin enabling kernel stability flag (in flight) 4) sam running a short perf run and flamegraph capture. monitor for 10 min.

incident-bot: INC-4521 update: mitigations applied. p95 dropped to ~210ms at 12:28 UTC. continuing to monitor for regressions. :eyes:

maria: great work. follow-up actions: PR-789 (perf regression root-cause), add guard in kernel-selector to avoid oscillation for tenants with >20k QPS. I'll post notes in the postmortem channel later. :thumbsup:
